geo.label: Hot CPI forces front-end repricing
parts: Macro Stance

January's consumer price report strengthened the case that the March lift-off the Fed signalled on January 26 (CNBC) [[n2152]] will be the first of several moves. Prices rose 7.5% from a year earlier, more than expected and the fastest pace since 1982, according to CNBC [[n2132]], and Bloomberg described a larger-than-forecast gain [[n2138]]. Reuters' wording matters most: inflation is becoming widespread [[n1196]], a broad-based pressure that policy has to lean against rather than look through. The labour market removes any excuse to wait after January payrolls rose by 467,000 (Al Jazeera) [[n2087]]. Our stance is Bearish for duration-sensitive US risk: the economy is strong, but the price of money is rising faster than earnings estimates can adjust.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y Treasury closed at 1.61% and the 10Y at 2.03%, a 10Y–2Y spread of +42 bps, with 10Y–3M at +163 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-10). Over twenty observations the 2Y rose +69 bps from 0.92% while the 10Y rose +29 bps from 1.74%, so the spread moved -40 bps: a bear flattening (both up, 2Y up more) on a curve that is still positively sloped. The front end did the work, adding +42 bps to the 2Y in five observations against +21 bps on the 10Y. CNBC reported the 10Y topping 2% for the first time since 2019 [[n2192]]. Reuters' explainer on the flattening curve is the right frame [[n2198]], because when the short end leads, financial conditions tighten through mortgage and corporate borrowing costs before the curve says anything about recession.
New / Most Important

Equities absorbed the shock unevenly. The S&P 500 fell -1.81% to 4,504.08 index points and the Nasdaq 100 -2.33% to 14,705.64, while the VIX jumped +19.79%, or +3.95 points, to 23.91 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). The US Dollar Index barely moved, +0.06% at 95.55 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), so markets read the print as a Fed-path shock rather than a dollar-funding one. Reuters reported that hot inflation fuels the case for a 'big-bang' Fed hike in March [[n2201]], but the Fed's Barkin said he would have to be convinced of the need for a half-point move [[n1363]]. Mortgage rates surged to a two-year high, with the 30-year at 3.69% (Orange County Register) [[n2135]], which pulls the rate shock straight into housing demand.
Playbook ✓

Action: run US equities underweight duration: trim long-dated growth, real estate and utilities, and fund cash-generative financials, energy and short-dated Treasuries. Trigger: the 2Y holding above 1.61% with the 10Y above 2% confirms the faster hiking path, and another leg of bear flattening extends the underweight. What changes the call: softer inflation data (Fortune argues inflation likely peaked months ago [[n2131]]) or more officials echoing Barkin's resistance to a half-point start would let the front end rally and reopen the growth trade. A VIX retreat toward its 17.62 reading of twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10) would be the confirming signal.

geo.label: ECB pushback versus energy-led inflation
parts: Macro Stance

Europe sits between two ECB messages. After the February 3 meeting Lagarde was no longer ruling out a rate hike this year (Al Jazeera) [[n1233]], yet days later she said there was no need for big tightening because inflation would hold at target (Yahoo Finance UK) [[n1276]]. Reuters' conclusion that the ECB 'put' for euro-zone bond markets is some way off [[n1322]] is the operative one: the bank will not lean early against wider spreads. Our stance is Mixed, supportive for banks and value, hostile for duration and periphery bonds.
Activity & Inflation

Price pressure is still energy-led. Eurostat figures published by the European Commission show energy prices rising across the euro area in 2021 [[n1321]], Dutch inflation hit its highest in 40 years (IamExpat) [[n1325]], and Bankier noted that European inflation surprised economists again [[n1605]]. Dutch TTF gas closed at 74.35 EUR/MWh, -7.32% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), a relief for industry that does not undo the household shock already locked in: EDF Energy will lift UK bills by an average £693 a year after the price-cap rise (Money Saving Expert) [[n2185]].
New / Most Important

Local indexes were steady: the STOXX 600 slipped -0.21% to 472.35 index points and the DAX added +0.05% to 15,490.44 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). European cash markets close before the US session ends, so the USD-listed VGK, -1.28% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), captures more of the CPI shock than the local benchmarks do. Geopolitics is the overlay: Chancellor Scholz told Russia not to underestimate 'our resolve' (DW) [[n1331]], while Ukraine insists Nord Stream 2 should never open (Sky News) [[n1329]].
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer European banks and energy over long-duration growth and core bonds. Trigger: continued outperformance of the Euro Stoxx 50, -2.75% over twenty sessions, against the Nasdaq 100 at -7.54% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), alongside an ECB that tolerates higher yields. What changes the call: a signal of ECB spread protection, or a Russian escalation that pushes TTF back above its 75.15 EUR/MWh level of twenty sessions ago, squeezing margins faster than higher rates lift bank earnings.

geo.label: Easing bias, property triage
parts: Macro Stance

China is the one major economy actively easing while the Fed prepares to tighten, and that divergence is the investable fact. The PBOC cut key lending rates, including one for the first time in nearly 2 years (CNBC) [[n0132]], and Bloomberg framed the move as the central bank seizing the moment for stimulus while the Fed hikes [[n0137]]. The growth base is respectable but losing speed: GDP grew 8.1% in 2021, the fastest in a decade (Global Times) [[n0126]], yet fixed-asset investment rose only 4.9% (Macau Business) [[n0128]]. We hold a Mixed stance because easing is real while its transmission runs through a property sector still in triage.
PMIs & Activity

The Caixin manufacturing PMI showed January factory activity contracting as COVID lockdowns bit (Reuters) [[n0142]]. Mass-market consumer signals point the same way, although premium spending is holding up: Coty reported strong results boosted by China (Asia Financial) [[n0206]] and Swire Properties sees luxury mall revenue growing across China (The Business of Fashion) [[n0217]]. CNBC reported the holiday box office plunging by 23% as theatres pushed ticket prices to records [[n0204]], an early sign that household demand is price-sensitive even in a holiday week, and Bloomberg's explainer on why some Chinese are 'lying flat' [[n0261]] adds a social dimension to that restraint. Industrial profits rebounded in 2021 (China Daily) [[n0140]], so margins entered the slowdown from strength, which buys policymakers time rather than forcing urgency.
Credit Impulse

The policy signal is easing, but credit transmission is selective. Beyond the benchmark-rate cuts, the PBOC cut rates on medium-term loans and reverse repos (Fibre2Fashion) [[n0135]], while regulators fined Ant-backed MYBank for violating credit-scoring rules (Reuters) [[n0184]] and the central bank tightened rules on cash withdrawals and deposits to target money laundering (Global Times) [[n0249]]. The combination is deliberate: cheaper money for approved channels, tighter supervision for platform and shadow credit. BNP Paribas Asset Management argues China's debt vulnerability keeps defying dire predictions [[n0157]], which is the bull case for the impulse; the bear case is that developers and households, not banks, are the bottleneck, and lower rates do little when borrowers will not borrow.
Property

Property remains the blockage. Reuters, citing a report, said China is giving property firms easier access to escrow funds [[n0245]], which, if confirmed, would be the most practical step so far because it would release developers' own presale cash instead of adding leverage. Evergrande aims to deliver 600,000 apartments in 2022 and says there will be no fire sales (Reuters) [[n0235]], and it vowed to finish half of the units under construction this year (Caixin Global) [[n0254]]. Governance questions undercut the plan: WSJ and the South China Morning Post reported that Evergrande's CEO sold bonds before the profit warning and default [[n0252]][[n0253]]. Nikkei Asia's 'ghost towns' report [[n0234]] is a reminder that unsold inventory, not just funding, caps new starts, even though December new-home prices fell less on promotions and easing curbs (Business Recorder) [[n0123]].
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Trade policy is opening a second front. China suspended Lithuanian beef, dairy and beer imports as the Taiwan row grew (Reuters) [[n0248]], and Taiwan, Canada and Japan asked to join the EU's WTO case against China (Politico Europe) [[n1484]]. With Washington the scorecard is poor: CNN reported China missed the trade targets it promised to Trump [[n0203]], and the Peterson Institute found China bought none of the extra $200 billion of US exports in the deal [[n0202]]. Volumes are still large, with 2021 imports and exports topping $6 trillion for the first time (Pandaily) [[n0122]], and Beijing plans to raise iron ore output and use more steel scrap (Reuters) [[n0045]]. Politically, China joined Russia in opposing NATO expansion (BBC) [[n1375]], raising the risk that Western sanctions on Russia spill into secondary-trade pressure on Chinese exporters.
Markets & Flows

Hong Kong is pricing the easing faster than the mainland. The Hang Seng closed at 24,924.35 index points, +4.96% over twenty sessions, while the Shanghai Composite at 3,485.91 is -2.79% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Tencent is +10.12% over twenty sessions at 460.07 HKD, and Bloomberg reported Didi shares climbing as Tencent boosted its stake [[n0802]]. US-listed proxies traded the CPI shock instead: FXI fell -1.21% and KWEB -1.64%, and Alibaba rose +2.86% in Hong Kong while its ADR fell -1.99% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Genuine flow channels are widening, with XPeng's shares included in the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect (XPeng) [[n0634]], while US regulatory risk persists after the Hang Seng slipped as WuXi Biologics sank by a record following its addition to a US red-flag list (South China Morning Post) [[n0210]].
New / Most Important

The new element, per the Reuters report, is that easing may be reaching developers' cash flow rather than only benchmark rates. Combined with the PBOC's stimulus stance, that improves the odds of completed-project deliveries, which is what restores buyer confidence. The counterweight is external: ASML flagged possible IP infringement by a 'little giant' in China (South China Morning Post) [[n0241]], a reminder that technology friction can tighten while domestic policy loosens, and XPeng's first European retail store (CNBC) [[n0795]] shows the export ambition that trade disputes can derail.
Playbook ✓

Action: own Hong Kong-listed platform exposure selectively, Tencent over the US-listed KWEB basket, and avoid private-developer credit. Trigger: further property-funding steps that build on the escrow change, with the Hang Seng holding its +4.96% twenty-session gain and the Shanghai Composite ending its underperformance. What changes the call: another major developer default, or a Lithuania-style trade dispute that pulls the EU into retaliation. ⚠ Divergence: policy is easing and Hong Kong is rallying, yet the Caixin PMI showed contraction [[n0142]] and the holiday box office fell 23% [[n0204]], so equity markets are front-running a demand recovery that activity data have not confirmed.

geo.label: Negative rates, chip-constrained exporters
parts: Macro Stance

Japan remains the policy outlier on the easy side. The BoJ has applied its minus interest rate to MUFG Bank's deposits (Asahi Shimbun) [[n1518]], even as Reuters reported internal debate on how to message an eventual rate hike as inflation perks up [[n1497]]. Wages explain the patience: The Japan Times asks why Japan's wages aren't rising [[n1532]], and Reuters' profile of a frugal family shows the limits of stimulus [[n1521]]. Our stance is Mixed: cost-push inflation is arriving through items like the Cup Noodle price hike (Reuters) [[n1508]], but without wage growth it erodes real income rather than justifying tighter policy.
Activity & Currency

December exports and imports hit records by value as supply bottlenecks eased (Reuters) [[n1499]], but record imports on surging energy prices (The Seattle Times) [[n1500]] mean the terms-of-trade loss runs through the currency: with the US 10Y at 2.03% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-10) and the BoJ still applying negative rates, the yen loses rate support without any BoJ move. Corporate signals split on chip access. Toyota's profit fell as the chip shortage hit production (BBC) [[n0700]] and its shares fell -2.74% to 2,254.00 JPY, while Nissan raised its profit outlook but sees chips limiting growth (Reuters) [[n1111]]. Chip-equipment makers rallied in the last completed Tokyo session, which ended before the US CPI release: Advantest +2.78% to 9,600.00 JPY and Tokyo Electron +1.82% to 57,150.00 JPY (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Playbook ✓

Action: favour semiconductor-equipment exporters over domestic automakers. Trigger: the 10Y Treasury holding above 2% while Advantest and Tokyo Electron keep their February 10 gains. What changes the call: the USD-listed EWJ fell -1.59% after the CPI shock (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), so the next Tokyo session has to absorb it; if the equipment makers then lag Toyota, the rate shock is overwhelming the chip cycle. SoftBank's mounting woes (The New York Times) [[n0849]] argue against using it as a growth proxy.

geo.label: QE ends, hike debate opens
parts: Macro Stance

Australia is ending QE with a murky future for $650b of assets (SMH) [[n0074]], following the RBA's February policy statement (Reserve Bank of Australia) [[n0016]]. The data argue for an earlier pivot: inflation spiked to 3.5 per cent (AFR) [[n0009]], which the AFR says will force an RBA interest rate pivot [[n0010]], and the jobless rate hit a 13-year low (The Australian) [[n0004]]. Our stance is Mixed: the economy is strong enough to absorb hikes, but a housing-heavy household balance sheet makes the first move a growth risk.
Demand & Financing

Bank results show where the leverage sits. Commonwealth Bank reported a first-half profit surge on the home boom and unveiled a share buyback (Reuters) [[n0054]], and The Australian reported CBA bullish on the economy as rate hikes loom [[n0662]]. CBA rose +1.23% to 100.78 AUD and is +7.86% over five sessions, while the S&P/ASX 200 added +0.28% to 7,288.50 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Reopening is the next demand impulse, with borders opening to vaccinated tourists on February 21 (Al Jazeera) [[n0043]]. Miners carry the external risk: Rio Tinto is +10.90% over twenty sessions at 118.96 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), but China's plan to raise domestic iron ore output (Reuters) [[n0045]] caps the upside.
Playbook ✓

Action: hold Australian banks over long-duration defensives such as CSL, -10.39% over twenty sessions at 253.71 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Trigger: RBA language that brings forward the first hike while employment stays tight. What changes the call: a hit to house prices or rents as international travel resumes, which ABC notes could affect the two in different ways [[n0057]], or an iron ore slide that hits the terms of trade. The USD-listed EWA, -0.91% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), points to a softer local open.

geo.label: Hawkish NBP, strong zloty, frontline risk
parts: Macro Stance

Poland has moved from behind the curve to openly hawkish. The Monetary Policy Council raised rates again, taking them to their highest in almost 9 years (Rzeczpospolita) [[n1723]], after Pekao had forecast a 50 bp move (StockWatch.pl) [[n1625]]. Governor Glapiński then cast himself as a hawk at an unusual press conference ('Ja jako jastrząb', Interia Wydarzenia) [[n1737]] and PolsatNews.pl ran the line 'I will urge tightening of monetary policy' over the question of whether loan instalments will rise further [[n1762]]. The backdrop justifies it: inflation exceeded 8% and hit a 21-year high (Bankier.pl) [[n1581]], and the end-2021 reading rose to 8.6% (300Gospodarka.pl) [[n1589]]. Labour is tight, with registered unemployment at 5.6% in January (RadioMaryja.pl, citing the family and social policy ministry) [[n1619]] and the average wage up 9.6% in 2021 (pb.pl) [[n1761]]. Our stance is Mixed: credible tightening and a strong currency against fiscal noise and frontline security risk.
Markets

Currency and equities are sending opposite messages. Bankier.pl reported the zloty at its strongest in 8 months [[n1785]] and credited Glapiński with strengthening it [[n1759]]. Warsaw equities have not followed: the Beta ETF WIG20TR fell -0.88% to 38.15 PLN on February 10 and is -8.09% over twenty sessions, while the USD-listed EPOL fell -2.27% to 21.13 USD in the US session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Bankier.pl is already asking whether markets are still in a correction or already in a bear phase [[n1777]]. Banks are where higher rates should pay: Parkiet argues WSE bank quotations have the potential to continue their bull run [[n1791]], but PKO Bank Polski fell -1.73% to 48.15 PLN and is -3.27% over twenty sessions, while Bank Pekao is -0.18% at 136.20 PLN over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). A strong currency alongside flat bank stocks says investors are discounting regulatory and geopolitical risk, not rates.
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal policy is the weak flank. Experts quoted by Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK call Polski Ład unfixable and want an entirely new law [[n1654]], Polityka.pl reports that Finance Minister Tadeusz Kościński was made an example of over the reform [[n1675]], and Wyborcza.biz says the next finance minister will be a woman [[n1719]]. A Business Insider Polska poll measuring how many people understand Polski Ład [[n1765]] keeps the reform's comprehension problem in public view. Inflation flatters the debt arithmetic, which Rzeczpospolita says helps the government manage state debt [[n1664]], but it also lifts indexation: pension indexation will be higher than forecast [[n1766]], even as purchasing power may fall [[n1767]]. In Brussels, the EU is withholding funds from Poland over an unpaid fine (The Guardian) [[n1568]] in the coal-mine dispute (DW) [[n1567]], Rzeczpospolita reports the government drawing lessons on whether Upper Silesian mines could become new Turów cases [[n1784]], and Politico Europe described a half step back to cool legal conflicts with the EU [[n1558]].
Corporate & Sectors

Energy costs dominate corporate news. Money.pl reports entrepreneurs alarmed by letters announcing gas supply restrictions [[n1795]], Business Insider Polska says bakers facing gas price rises of up to 1000% wrote to the prime minister [[n1622]], and WysokieNapiecie.pl notes that gas for business quietly became cheaper [[n1744]], a sign the worst of the contract reset may be passing. Orlen raised wholesale fuel prices (INNPoland.pl) [[n1715]], its CEO says Lotos jobs will be kept (Bankier.pl) [[n1722]], and MOL's deputy chief says the Hungarian group will become one of the most important players (Rzeczpospolita) [[n1768]]. Orlen fell -2.78% to 71.22 PLN and is -12.55% over twenty sessions, while KGHM rose +4.63% to 152.40 PLN and JSW is +20.79% over twenty sessions at 48.80 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10); KGHM has registered its copper cathodes on China's INE exchange (Inwestycje.pl) [[n1713]]. Consumers are the pressure point: LPP is optimistic about the year but expects cost pressure to hit margins (Bankier.pl) [[n1671]], and its shares are -14.12% over twenty sessions, with Allegro -20.91% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Geopolitics & Security

Poland is now NATO's frontline logistics hub. The first US reinforcement troops have arrived (Reuters) [[n1548]], US troops in Poland are preparing for Americans potentially fleeing Ukraine (Reuters) [[n1574]], US aircraft are heading to Poland to enhance collective defence (European Command) [[n1580]], and the UK is sending 350 more troops to the Polish border (Politico Europe) [[n1562]]; Prime Minister Morawiecki called Britain's move a wonderful proof of solidarity (Gov.pl) [[n1799]]. Diplomatically, Poland, as OSCE head, says political will is needed to end the standoff (Reuters) [[n1577]]. The danger is that markets treat security as binary: Russia and Belarus began military drills near Belarus's border with Ukraine (The Guardian) [[n1478]], a survey reported by Bankier.pl finds Europeans fear Russia will attack Ukraine this year [[n1742]], and TVN24 reports people arriving from all over Ukraine to prepare to defend the country [[n1771]].
New / Most Important

The decisive development is hawkish NBP communication turning into currency strength, because a firmer zloty is the cheapest disinflation tool Poland has. Glapiński also intends to buy another 100 tonnes of gold (Business Insider Polska) [[n1739]], diversifying reserves while regional risk rises. Biznes Wprost had noted first signals of falling inflation as the zloty awaited the decision [[n1735]], and Credit Agricole's revised forecast of 7.5% inflation this year and 5.5% next year (Bankier.pl) [[n1592]] shows how long the overshoot is expected to last. Higher real-rate expectations, a firmer currency and reserve accumulation form the macro case for Polish assets; geopolitics is the reason it is not yet priced into equities.
Playbook ✓

Action: express the hawkish NBP through the currency and short-dated domestic rates rather than broad Warsaw equities, and within equities favour commodity exporters such as KGHM and JSW over consumer names. Trigger: the zloty holding its eight-month high while the WIG20TR tracker stops falling from 38.15 PLN. What changes the call: a Russian escalation that lifts regional risk premia, or a fiscal response to Polski Ład that undoes the NBP's work. ⚠ Divergence: the zloty sits at an eight-month high on NBP hawkishness, yet EPOL is -8.57% and the WIG20TR tracker -8.09% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), so the currency market is pricing policy credibility while equity holders are pricing war and regulatory risk.
Narrative

Technology is the sector most exposed to the front-end repricing. XLK fell -2.61% to 159.77 USD and is -5.32% over twenty sessions, with Microsoft -2.84% and Apple -2.36% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). JP Morgan warned that the tech sell-off may continue for another month (The Edge Malaysia) [[n0461]].
Reported

The reported news is structural rather than cyclical. Nvidia and SoftBank terminated Nvidia's acquisition of Arm (NVIDIA Newsroom) [[n1078]], AMD set an all-time CPU market-share record as Intel gained in desktops and notebooks (Tom's Hardware) [[n0647]], and Intel launched a $1 billion fund to build a foundry innovation ecosystem (Intel) [[n1887]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside sits with companies that turn efficiency into margin: WSJ reported Microsoft kept its finance head count flat using AI and bots [[n1181]]. Apple's new way to buy things by tapping iPhones together (CNBC) [[n1092]] extends the existing iPhone base into payments, though revenue is unquantified.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention says quality tech is a refuge in a sell-off. Not when the discount rate moves this fast: Apple and Microsoft de-rate alongside speculative names. Dispersion inside software, Datadog +12.28% against Adobe -5.12% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), shows the market paying only for visible near-term growth.
Narrative

Communication services split between content winners and ad-model losers. XLC fell -1.43% to 70.84 USD and is -8.01% over twenty sessions, dragged by Meta Platforms (FB), -31.56% over that window at 228.07 USD, while Walt Disney rose +3.35% to 152.16 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Reported

Disney+ added 11.8 million subscribers with a strong forecast (TechCrunch) [[n1171]], and Reuters said streaming growth and park revenue boosted the shares [[n0682]]. Twitter's stock swung to a gain despite underwhelming user growth because of a new $4 billion buyback (MarketWatch) [[n0861]].
EPS Upside Watch

Parks are Disney's cleaner earnings lever, since Reuters says the streaming industry's future is still in question even as Disney closes the gap with Netflix [[n0803]]. The Discovery-WarnerMedia deal cleared US antitrust review (Reuters) [[n0675]], creating a larger rival for subscribers and content.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The old convention treats Meta, Snap and Pinterest as one digital-advertising trade. Forbes' look at the $10 billion impact of privacy changes on Apple and Meta [[n0787]] shows why that fails: the owner of the operating system now shapes who wins. Snap is +65.80% over five sessions while Meta Platforms (FB) is -4.08% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), so the sector needs stock picking, not beta.
Narrative

Financials are the relative winner from higher short rates. XLF fell only -0.88% to 40.68 USD and is -1.79% over twenty sessions against -4.70% for the S&P 500, with Wells Fargo +4.70% and Bank of America +0.39% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Reported

Reported news favours capital returns: KKR's earnings fell while cash available to shareholders hit new heights (WSJ) [[n0573]], ABN Amro shares slipped because its buyback underwhelmed (Reuters) [[n1353]], and Morgan Stanley agreed to buy Cook Street Consulting (Barron's) [[n0829]].
EPS Upside Watch

Net interest income is the lever. Kansas City Fed research on how margins at small and large banks respond to rates [[n2196]] is directly relevant with the 2Y at 1.61% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-10); our working assumption is that asset yields reprice faster than deposit costs. Wells Fargo asking staff back to the office in mid-March (Reuters) [[n0764]] signals operating confidence.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Convention says a flattening curve hurts banks. With 10Y–2Y still at +42 bps and 10Y–3M at +163 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-10), the level of short rates matters more than the slope. The bigger risk is legal: customers are suing Bank of America for not refunding pandemic overdraft fees (Reuters) [[n0800]].
Narrative

Energy is the market's inflation hedge of choice. XLE is +8.00% over twenty sessions at 68.42 USD, with Brent at 91.41 USD/bbl (+7.96%) and WTI at 89.88 USD/bbl (+8.76%) over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Strategists see oil hitting $100 on strong demand and the Russia-Ukraine crisis (Reuters) [[n1377]].
Reported

Energy prices lifted BP's profits to an eight-year high (Reuters) [[n0558]], Equinor published its fourth-quarter results (Equinor) [[n0694]], and Morningstar explains why energy stocks are gushing high dividends [[n0766]].
EPS Upside Watch

Capital discipline is the upside: OilPrice.com argues shale growth may not materialise as producers run out of sweet spots [[n1891]], supporting price without volume risk. Occidental is +17.06% and Exxon Mobil +9.98% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), and the cash returns behind those moves do not need a higher oil price, only a stable one.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The contrarian risk is supply from diplomacy, not weaker demand: Iran's oil exports are increasing as nuclear talks resume (Reuters) [[n1464]]. A deal would hit the geopolitical premium before it touches earnings, so hold the producers, not the leveraged oil-price expression.
Narrative

Industrials are torn between pricing power in logistics and cost pressure in manufacturing. XLI fell -1.64% to 100.90 USD and is -5.04% over twenty sessions; Boeing rose +1.34% to 218.75 USD while Caterpillar is -8.69% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Reported

Maersk reported record 2021 earnings with profit up threefold (Indonesia Shipping Gazette) [[n0715]], Boeing deliveries remain low as 787 problems weigh (Reuters) [[n0540]], and Frontier agreed to buy Spirit Airlines in a $2.9 bln budget-carrier deal (Reuters) [[n0447]].
EPS Upside Watch

Capital is flowing to scarce capacity: Republic Services agreed to acquire US Ecology (PR Newswire) [[n1151]], and FedEx is eyeing a freighter order as e-commerce soars (Reuters) [[n0562]]. Those are the order books that convert inflation into revenue rather than into margin loss.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention frames industrials as a reopening trade. The better frame is scarcity: The New York Times reported a normal supply chain is unlikely in 2022 [[n1865]], which keeps freight and logistics earnings elevated even if goods demand cools, and leaves machinery makers exposed to input costs.
Narrative

Consumer discretionary carries both the rate shock and the real-income shock. XLY fell -1.72% to 185.82 USD and is -7.78% over twenty sessions; Tesla fell -2.95% to 904.55 USD and Amazon -1.36% to 3,180.07 USD, although Amazon is still +14.52% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Reported

Chipotle's small-town expansion is fuelling record profit (MarketWatch) [[n0669]], Yum Brands' sales were boosted by demand for tacos and fried chicken (Reuters) [[n0708]], and Harley-Davidson's results topped forecasts as motorcycle demand soared (Reuters) [[n1099]].
EPS Upside Watch

Pricing power is the upside lever: Chipotle's menu prices are about 10% higher than a year ago and still climbing (Restaurant Dive) [[n1135]], and Starbucks, Chipotle and other big chains have price hikes on the menu (MONEY) [[n1150]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention says strong earnings protect the stock. Amazon's record $191 billion market-value jump (Bloomberg) [[n0082]] came alongside a Prime price hike (CBS News) [[n2166]], while Tesla is recalling 579,000 cars (Kelley Blue Book) [[n1981]]. Consumer names are being paid for price, not volume, and that ends when real incomes crack.
Narrative

Staples reveal who can pass on inflation. XLP fell -1.07% to 75.52 USD and is -1.60% over twenty sessions, a defensive outperformance, but Coca-Cola rose +0.56% to 61.38 USD while PepsiCo fell -2.08% to 168.37 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Reported

Coca-Cola beat estimates as demand for drinks away from home topped pre-pandemic levels (CNBC) [[n0798]], and Reuters reported that Coca-Cola and PepsiCo both warned of an inflation bite even as higher prices lifted sales [[n0799]]. Inflation is turning up the heat on Unilever even as it backs down on M&A (Reuters) [[n0821]].
EPS Upside Watch

Kellogg joined Chipotle and Starbucks in planning price hikes (Forbes) [[n1178]], but its labour strike will eat into margins as supply woes mount (Reuters) [[n0709]]. Upside requires price increases to stick without volume loss.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Staples are usually bought as bond proxies, which fails when yields rise. The sector now works only where volume holds after price increases: Coca-Cola's away-from-home recovery is volume, PepsiCo's warning is cost, and the spread between the two is the trade rather than the sector ETF.
Narrative

Health care is losing its COVID tailwind just as rates punish biotech. XLV fell -1.57% to 132.08 USD, Moderna is -28.03% over twenty sessions at 160.42 USD, and XBI fell -2.98% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Reported

AstraZeneca sees higher 2022 sales even as the COVID boost wanes (Reuters) [[n1963]], CVS forecast its COVID vaccine business could drop by up to 80% in 2022 (Reuters) [[n0663]], and Pfizer forecast $100B in sales fuelled by its vaccine and pill (BioPharma Dive) [[n1117]], yet its forecasts missed estimates and the shares fell 4% (The Peninsula Qatar) [[n0599]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside rotates to non-COVID franchises: tirzepatide won as an add-on to insulin glargine (MedPage Today) [[n1919]], and AbbVie's Qulipta is gaining ground with doctors for migraine prevention (Fierce Pharma) [[n0782]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Health care is usually the safe defensive. The hidden constraint is funding: BioPharma Dive reported the biotech rout has left drug startups grounded as demand slumps for IPOs [[n1344]], so small-cap biotech behaves like long-duration tech, and the defensive part of the sector is narrower than the ETF suggests.
Narrative

Materials are split between scarce metals and rate-sensitive chemicals. XLB fell -0.58% to 85.32 USD and is -5.47% over twenty sessions, while Alcoa is +15.01% at 71.17 USD and aluminum futures +11.61% at 3,319.00 USD/t over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Reported
DuPont beat profit estimates on price hikes and electronics demand (Reuters) [[n0554]], and ArcelorMittal reported its fourth-quarter and full-year 2021 results (ArcelorMittal) [[n1166]].
EPS Upside Watch

Supply tightness is the upside: Reuters columnist Andy Home writes that a surge in LME stocks failed to cool the red-hot aluminium market [[n0243]], and Mining.com reports global copper stocks down to three days' consumption [[n1936]]. Producers with spare smelting capacity hold the pricing power.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention links materials to Chinese demand. Here the driver is disruption: MMG is halting the Las Bambas copper mine amid a fresh blockade (Mining.com) [[n1889]], and Agnico Eagle and Kirkland Lake Gold sealed their merger (Northern Ontario Business) [[n0652]]. Supply events and consolidation, not growth, are setting prices and multiples.
Narrative

Real estate is the cleanest casualty of the 10Y crossing 2%. XLRE fell -2.85% to 46.05 USD and is -6.08% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), with the 10Y closing at 2.03% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-10).
Reported

Zillow's shuttered home-flipping business lost $881 million in 2021 (WSJ) [[n0882]], and Yahoo Finance reports that new homeowners are being rushed into buying and that 75% of them feel they got a raw deal [[n0726]]. Opendoor fell -2.00% to 10.29 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
EPS Upside Watch

Rents are the offset: Realtor.com says the US housing supply gap expanded in 2021 [[n2114]], which should keep occupancy and pricing firm for landlords even if transaction volumes slow. Residential landlords with short leases can reprice rents faster than office or retail owners locked into long contracts.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Consensus treats housing as late-cycle but resilient. Mortgage rates surged to their highest point since Jan. 2020 (Realtor.com) [[n2134]], and household debt jumped by $1 trillion in 2021, the most since 2007 (CNN) [[n2108]], so affordability, not supply, becomes the binding constraint and REIT multiples have further to adjust.
Narrative

Utilities traded as bond proxies. XLU fell -2.53% to 66.99 USD, with Duke Energy -4.70% to 99.79 USD and Southern Company -3.13% to 65.95 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). XLU is -3.67% over twenty sessions and NextEra Energy -11.33% over the same window, so the sell-off is about the discount rate, not any single regulatory decision.
Reported
Duke Energy expanded its clean energy action plan (Duke Energy News Center) [[n0690]], and Barron's describes Berkshire Hathaway's utility business as a crown jewel [[n0507]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside depends on rate-base growth outrunning financing costs. TotalEnergies' purchase of SunPower's commercial and industrial business for $250 mln (Reuters) [[n0859]] shows strategic buyers paying for renewable platforms, which supports asset values but not regulated returns. Allowed returns would have to reset higher before valuations stabilise, and regulators move slowly.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Convention says utilities hedge equity drawdowns. When the drawdown is caused by rising yields, they fall with growth, as they did on February 10. Macron's bet on new nuclear reactors (Reuters) [[n1975]] is a policy tailwind for generators and fuel suppliers, not for regulated bond proxies.
Narrative

European autos price a chip-supply recovery against a weak production base. The STOXX 600 autos tracker (EXV5.DE) fell -0.36% to 61.71 EUR and is -6.44% over twenty sessions; Mercedes-Benz Group is -7.53% at 69.75 EUR and BMW -6.31% at 92.77 EUR, while Renault is +7.72% at 36.50 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Reported

ACEA expects EU car sales to rise 7.9% in 2022 as chip supply stabilises (Reuters) [[n1879]], while Obserwator Gospodarczy reports German car production is still falling and is 40% below its level three years ago [[n1800]].
EPS Upside Watch

Mix and price are carrying margins: Stellantis launched the electrified Alfa Romeo Tonale SUV (Reuters) [[n0612]], and CarExpert's C-Class supply update, with no plug-in hybrid at launch [[n0777]], shows how constrained supply is shaping the model mix.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The new competitor is Chinese: XPeng is expanding into Sweden and the Netherlands (Reuters) [[n0796]], and CarAndBike lists five European automotive brands now owned by Chinese companies [[n1883]]. A supply recovery that arrives alongside new entrants transfers pricing power back to buyers.
Narrative

Semiconductors split by time zone. In Asia, SK Hynix rose +5.28% to 129,500.00 KRW, Samsung Electronics +3.29% to 75,400.00 KRW and TAIEX +1.03%, all before the US CPI release; in New York, SOXX fell -3.12% to 488.90 USD and the PHLX Semiconductor Index -3.22% to 3,536.10 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Reported

Samsung's newest Galaxy S smartphones have a faster chip (Reuters) [[n0840]], ASML said it supports the European Chip Act proposal (Reuters) [[n0521]] and flagged that a Chinese rival might be infringing its IP (Taipei Times) [[n0781]].
EPS Upside Watch

Memory is the upside lever: Micron rose +3.29% to 91.02 USD against the US sell-off, while the TSMC ADR fell only -0.65% to 124.71 USD and ASML's US line -3.45% to 656.88 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Lam Research introduced selective etch tools to accelerate chipmakers' 3D roadmaps (Yahoo Finance) [[n0712]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Automakers and chip firms differ on when the shortage will abate (Reuters) [[n1025]]. If the carmakers are right about an earlier end, the pricing power that has supported analog and auto-chip margins fades first, while memory and equipment hold up.

earnings_pattern.title: Pricing power and buybacks paid, distant profits punished
parts: Rewarded

Walt Disney rose +3.35% to 152.16 USD after earnings topped estimates as Disney+ subscriptions surged (Al Jazeera) [[n0681]]; Variety reported Disney Plus ended 2021 with nearly 130 million subscribers, smashing growth forecasts [[n0679]]. Coca-Cola gained +0.56% to 61.38 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10) after beating estimates (CNBC) [[n0798]]. Twitter's shares swung to a gain because a buyback outweighed weak user numbers [[n0861]]. By contrast, Zynga's record results left its stock mostly unmoved after hours because the pending Take-Two acquisition anchors the price (MarketWatch) [[n0883]].
Punished

Uber fell -6.07% to 37.75 USD as its 2024 profit forecast fell short of expectations (Reuters) [[n0864]]; WSJ said the outlook left investors hungry for more [[n0865]]. PepsiCo fell -2.08% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10) after it joined Coca-Cola in warning of an inflation bite (Reuters) [[n0799]]. Delivery Hero's shares were punished as earnings disappointed (Reuters) [[n1186]], and Seagen sank as the sales outlook for a cancer drug disappointed (BioPharma Dive) [[n1189]]. Affirm (AFRM) lost -21.42% to 58.68 USD in the same session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10).
Pattern

The common thread is the duration of profits. Companies showing current pricing power or returning cash were rewarded; those asking investors to wait were sold. The Guardian noted that Uber's food delivery finally shows a profit [[n0866]], yet the stock still fell, which suggests near-term improvement does not compensate for a profit target several years out once the discount rate jumps. Coca-Cola's volume recovery and Disney's subscriber surprise are present-tense numbers.
Attention into EPS

Watch the language of profitability timelines. Twilio targets consistent profitability from 2023 (Light Reading) [[n0860]], and Zebit's exit highlights the challenges for the profitless buy-now-pay-later sector (Banking Day) [[n0878]]. With the 2Y at 1.61% and up +69 bps over twenty observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-10), every year of delay costs more, so guidance that pulls profit forward will be rewarded disproportionately.
Playbook

Action: buy post-earnings strength only where the beat comes from price or volume today and is reinforced by buybacks; fade rallies in companies whose guidance relies on out-year margins. Trigger: a beat accompanied by a raised near-term outlook. What changes the call: a decisive rally in the 2Y, which would lower the penalty on distant cash flows and revive long-duration growth names.

underowned.title: Uranium restart: Cameco and the fuel chain
parts: Attention Gap

Uranium rarely features in mainstream growth or value screens, yet Cameco plans to restart its McArthur River mine (Global News) [[n0664]], a supply decision that suggests confidence in contract pricing. Policy demand is building alongside it, with Macron betting on nuclear and announcing new reactors (Reuters) [[n1975]].
Exposure & Risk

Cameco (CCJ) is +17.15% over five sessions at 22.40 USD, the uranium ETF URA +10.94% at 22.10 USD and Centrus Energy +13.34% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). The risk is that a restart adds supply faster than utilities sign long-term contracts.
Trigger to Watch

Contracting announcements from utilities after the restart news, and whether URA can hold its five-session gain while long-duration equities fall. A failure to hold would show the move was momentum rather than a repricing of fuel scarcity.

underowned.title: Aluminium scarcity outside the spotlight
parts: Attention Gap

Metals attention centres on copper and gold, but aluminium is just as tight: Andy Home's column notes that a surge in LME stocks failed to cool the red-hot market (Reuters) [[n0243]], and Asia Financial traces how a single Chinese city became a global aluminium hub [[n0255]], a concentration risk that is easy to overlook.
Exposure & Risk

Aluminum futures closed at 3,319.00 USD/t, +7.76% over five sessions, and Alcoa is +13.44% over five sessions at 71.17 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). The risk is energy: smelters are power-intensive, so a gas-price collapse would ease the constraint quickly and remove the producers' margin cushion.
Trigger to Watch
Chinese output decisions and European power prices; a renewed TTF spike would tighten supply further and extend the trade.

underowned.title: Fertiliser and grains into planting season
parts: Attention Gap

Agriculture is the food-inflation channel that rate-focused portfolios tend to overlook. The USDA reported fertilizer prices spiking just ahead of the 2022 planting season [[n1938]], Successful Farming reported soybeans closing near $16 per bushel [[n1947]], and Farm Progress lists reasons wheat could be this year's big winner [[n1960]].
Exposure & Risk

Soybeans are +13.15% over twenty sessions at 1,574.25 US cents/bu and corn +7.14% at 641.75 US cents/bu, while Mosaic is +9.57% and CF Industries +8.63% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). The risk is that USDA projects farm prices for major field crops to decline (USDA) [[n1882]].
Trigger to Watch
Black Sea supply risk around the Russia-Ukraine standoff, which would lift wheat and fertiliser together; a calmer outcome would leave the USDA's lower price projection as the base case.

underowned.title: Container logistics as a cash machine
parts: Attention Gap

Logistics earnings tend to be dismissed as a pandemic anomaly, yet FreightWaves says shipping giant Maersk could rake in $50 billion over just two years [[n0742]], and Maersk is acquiring Pilot Freight Services to boost landside transportation (Maersk) [[n1930]], recycling windfall cash into the supply chain.
Exposure & Risk

Exposure runs through Maersk, freight forwarders and integrated carriers. The risk is a normalisation of rates; The Guardian reports rising shipping costs are hitting UK firms [[n1992]], the kind of customer pain that eventually invites new capacity.
Trigger to Watch

Further vertical integration: Supply Chain Dive reports food suppliers wading into logistics as trucking rates soar [[n1939]], and FreightWaves says retailers are lining up to own trucking companies [[n1958]]. More buyers of capacity means rates stay high for longer.

crypto.title: Bitcoin's rebound meets the rate shock
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 43,565.11 USD, -1.74% on the day but +19.50% over twenty sessions, while Ether fell -5.00% to 3,077.48 USD and Solana -6.86% to 106.20 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-10). The rebound had momentum, with Al Jazeera reporting Bitcoin at $44,000 after five straight days of gains [[n0914]], but the CPI shock reasserted crypto's role as the longest-duration risk asset. Equity proxies amplified the move: Coinbase Global fell -4.54% and MicroStrategy -3.39%, while GBTC fell -3.37% and the futures-based BITO -1.74% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), so even regulated wrappers traded with the risk complex rather than as a hedge.
New / Most Important

Regulation and security dominate. The Block reported that Congress rejected Treasury's proposed stablecoin regime at a House hearing [[n0942]], Time described the chess match that led federal agents to $3.6 billion in stolen Bitcoin [[n0968]], Coinbase removed cryptocurrency links after 'rug pull' warnings (Reuters) [[n0963]], and another $10M was lost in a DeFi hack of Dego Finance (Yahoo Finance) [[n0962]]. Institutional plumbing keeps building: Canada's TMX Group plans a crypto futures product for institutional investors (Reuters) [[n0935]], Bill Miller says bitcoin miners trade at very attractive valuations (CNBC) [[n0953]], and FTX is giving away free bitcoin as part of its Super Bowl commercial (Ad Age) [[n0918]], a bid for mass attention that can lift volumes without changing the macro.
Playbook

Action: keep crypto exposure light and prefer Bitcoin over high-beta alternatives and listed miners until rates stabilise. Trigger: Bitcoin reclaiming $44,000 [[n0914]] while the 2Y stops rising would signal that the rebound can survive a hawkish Fed. What changes the call: a stablecoin framework that clears the way for bank participation, or a further rise in short yields that pushes Bitcoin back below its 36,457.32 USD level of twenty sessions ago, which would end the rebound thesis.

flows.title: Liquidity drains while dividends absorb the bond exodus
parts: Global Liquidity

The global liquidity regime is turning against risk. A Reuters commentary on a historic central bank drain questions the 'buy the dip' reflex [[n1361]], the Financial Times argues markets are losing trust in central banks [[n1355]], and The Economist warns the global interest bill is about to jump [[n0173]]. The offsets are partial: emerging markets signal an end to aggressive rate-raising cycles (Financial Times) [[n0101]], China's central bank is seizing the moment for stimulus (Bloomberg) [[n0137]], Australia is ending QE rather than tightening outright (SMH) [[n0074]], and the US Treasury cut its quarterly sale of long-term debt (Gulf Times) [[n0088]], which trims duration supply at the margin. The plumbing risk is margin: BNP Paribas research on the 'dash for cash' stresses leverage and the need for policy coordination [[n1334]], and the Bank of England's Jon Cunliffe set out lessons from that episode for margining practices [[n1316]], because forced selling to meet margin calls is how a rate shock becomes a liquidity event.
Rates & Dollar

The 10Y at 2.03% and the 2Y at 1.61% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-10) reprice every discount rate. The dollar index is +0.58% over twenty sessions at 95.55 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), a muted move because Europe is tightening its rhetoric too: Reuters reported the dollar and euro trading sideways after the ECB pushback [[n1267]], and CNBC described the two facing off in a rate-hike tussle [[n1253]]. Real yields are the bigger story, with the 30-year real yield rising above zero (tipswatch.com) [[n2169]]. Treasury ETFs show the damage by maturity: TLT -1.59%, IEF -0.92% and SHY -0.51% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). The transmission to households is already visible in mortgage rates at a two-year high of 3.69% (Orange County Register) [[n2135]].
Credit Check

Credit is falling with rates rather than on default fears. LQD fell -1.36% to 123.92 USD and is -4.60% over twenty sessions, worse than HYG at -1.32% and -4.08%, while EMB is -3.07% over twenty sessions at 102.96 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10); investment grade underperforming high yield over the window points to duration, not spread, as the driver. Primary markets are thinning, with 9fin's leveraged-finance wrap describing a paltry primary [[n1327]], and Syniverse and the SPAC M3-Brigade scrapped their $2.85 billion merger (Reuters) [[n1357]]. Richmond Fed work on how post-2008 regulation affected corporate bond liquidity [[n1359]] is a reminder that dealer balance sheets amplify selling, and Reuters' dashboard of emerging-market vulnerabilities to rising global rates [[n1337]] maps the next pressure points. In Chinese high yield, filings showing Evergrande's CEO dumped all his dollar bonds before default (South China Morning Post) [[n0253]] will make recovery-value investors demand a larger governance discount.
Equity & Fund Flows

The clearest flow signal is rotation within income: US dividend funds received huge inflows as investors switched out of bonds (Reuters) [[n1358]]. Corporate buybacks add support, with Amgen buying back $6 bln in shares this quarter (Reuters) [[n0533]] and Commonwealth Bank unveiling a buyback (Reuters) [[n0054]]. Growth exposure is being cut: Cathie Wood dumped $142 million of Twitter stock before earnings (Bloomberg) [[n0433]], and Yahoo Finance explains why Ark Innovation ETF stocks are getting pummeled [[n0628]]. Issuance is selective: Abu Dhabi Ports surged 15% in its debut after raising $1.1 billion (CNBC) [[n1346]], and D-Wave plans to go public via a $1.6 bln SPAC deal (Reuters) [[n1347]], while in Korea money is rushing to safer assets (KED Global) [[n1342]].
Portfolio Implication

Position for a liquidity drain, not a recession: overweight dividend-paying financials and energy, which match where flows are going; underweight long-duration growth and REITs; keep credit exposure short in maturity, since LQD's -4.60% twenty-session loss (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10) shows duration, not default, is what is being punished. Hold some gold and short-dated cash as the hedge that still works when bonds and equities fall together. The call changes if the front end rallies decisively, or if a geopolitical shock forces a flight to Treasuries strong enough to restore the bond-equity hedge; in that case long Treasuries become the better hedge again.

anticipatory.title: March FOMC: a quarter-point start or a half-point jolt
parts: What Is Priced

The 2Y at 1.61%, +69 bps over twenty observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-10), already embeds a fast start. Reuters reported that hot inflation fuels the case for a 'big-bang' hike in March [[n2201]], after an earlier Reuters analysis judged a start with a bang not likely [[n2161]]; the Fed had already indicated an increase in rates as inflation rose (The Guardian) [[n2153]].
Conditional Expression

If officials endorse a half-point move, expect further bear flattening and favour XLF over XLK, whose -5.32% twenty-session loss (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10) would extend. If they settle on a quarter-point start with a firm path, the front end can rally and the Nasdaq 100, -7.54% over twenty sessions, is the cleanest rebound expression.
Risk

Consensus is moving fast: a January Reuters poll had the Fed raising rates three times this year [[n2026]], and CME Group's review of rate-hike expectations versus reality [[n2157]] is a reminder that pricing can run ahead of delivery. A surprise in either direction would hit the most crowded duration trades first.

anticipatory.title: Russia-Belarus drills: escalation or a negotiated pause
parts: What Is Priced

Brent at 91.41 USD/bbl is +7.96% over twenty sessions, Rheinmetall +7.50% at 96.02 EUR and Lockheed Martin +6.68%, yet TTF fell -7.32% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Russia has begun massive military exercises in Belarus and the Black Sea (Axios) [[n1479]], and Liz Truss warned Russia of sanctions during tense talks (The Guardian) [[n1476]].
Conditional Expression

On escalation, own energy and defence and hedge European cyclicals and Polish assets; Ukraine already accuses Russia of a Black Sea blockade (Atlantic Council) [[n1467]]. A negotiated pause has a foothold, since Macron said Putin told him Russia won't escalate (PBS) [[n1300]]; in that case the gas premium would compress and European equities would rebound.
Risk

Sanctions mechanics cut both ways: banks face a compliance nightmare over looming Russia sanctions (Global Trade Review) [[n1441]], while The Conversation argues Russia probably won't turn off the gas [[n1489]]. The energy hedge can fail even in an escalation.

anticipatory.title: Iran nuclear deal: oil's supply wildcard
parts: What Is Priced

XLE is +8.00% over twenty sessions and WTI +8.76% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10), with strategists targeting $100 oil [[n1377]]. Supply is already leaking: Iran's oil exports are increasing as nuclear talks resume (Reuters) [[n1464]], after the US restored a sanctions waiver with talks in their final phase (Reuters) [[n1387]].
Conditional Expression

If a deal is reached, barrels return and the geopolitical premium compresses; rotate from producers toward fuel-sensitive airlines, where Frontier and Spirit are merging [[n0447]]. If talks fail, the premium holds and producers keep their cash-return advantage; refiners benefit in either case while diesel stays expensive, and a Reuters commentary calls diesel the US economy's inflation canary [[n2183]].
Risk

Signals conflict: Israel puts Iran's breakout time at four to six months even with a deal (Axios) [[n1447]], US lawmakers are pessimistic about a new agreement (Politico) [[n1461]], and Iran calls the removal of US sanctions its red line (France 24) [[n1409]]. Talks can stall for weeks, so time decay is the risk for option structures.

anticipatory.title: China property easing: from escrow to completions
parts: What Is Priced

Hong Kong has priced some relief, with the Hang Seng +4.96% and Tencent +10.12% over twenty sessions, while the Shanghai Composite is -2.79% and Fortescue rose +3.97% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Easier access to escrow funds, per a Reuters report [[n0245]], and Evergrande's aim to deliver 600,000 apartments in 2022 (Reuters) [[n0235]] are the visible catalysts, so the next move depends on execution rather than announcements.
Conditional Expression

If Beijing adds further developer-funding measures, extend into Hong Kong-listed consumer and platform names and Australian iron ore producers such as Rio Tinto, +10.90% over twenty sessions at 118.96 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). If developers keep missing deliveries, rotate back to the mainland's state-backed sectors and cut the miners first.
Risk

Hong Kong's own fifth COVID wave is denting home valuations (South China Morning Post) [[n0211]], and Mandarin Oriental's boss says its team is leaving Hong Kong over COVID restrictions (Radio Free Asia) [[n0259]]. A policy rally in a market where companies are moving staff out may not last beyond the first funding headlines.

catalysts.title: Walt Disney (DIS)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Disney crushed Wall Street expectations as Disney+ soared to nearly 130 million subscribers (The Hollywood Reporter) [[n0677]], adding 11.8 million in the quarter with a strong forecast [[n1171]]. Parks give earnings a present-tense driver that most streaming peers lack.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Disney rose +3.35% to 152.16 USD but remains -3.57% over twenty sessions from 157.80 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Risk: parks capacity remains limited by staff shortages (WDW News Today) [[n0678]].
Trade Expression

Buy while the stock holds above 152.16 USD; add on a close above 157.80 USD, which would erase the twenty-session loss. Exit if it falls back through the pre-earnings range, which would mean the market is again treating Disney as a streaming-only story.

catalysts.title: Uber Technologies (UBER)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Uber beat on revenue and said its core business is bouncing back after the omicron surge (CNBC) [[n0758]], but its 2024 profit forecast fell short of expectations [[n0864]]. The market is refusing to pay for distant profit targets.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock fell -6.07% to 37.75 USD and is -12.29% over twenty sessions from 43.04 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Upside risk: the Transplace acquisition is beginning to boost Uber Freight's bottom line (FreightWaves) [[n1195]], adding near-term earnings.
Trade Expression

Wait for stabilisation above 37.75 USD before buying; a recovery toward 43.04 USD needs a falling 2Y. Avoid adding while the front end keeps rising, because Uber's valuation still rests on profits several years out.

catalysts.title: Meta Platforms (FB)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Facebook suffered a $230bn wipeout in the biggest one-day US stock plunge (The Guardian) [[n0305]], and the overhangs keep growing: Meta says it may shut Facebook and Instagram in Europe over data sharing (CNBC) [[n1275]], though it has since clarified that threat (Fossbytes) [[n1130]], and Peter Thiel is leaving its board (Silicon Republic) [[n1115]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Meta Platforms (FB) fell -1.69% to 228.07 USD and is -31.56% over twenty sessions from 333.26 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Upside risk: a cheap valuation can attract value buyers on any privacy-impact clarity.
Trade Expression

Stay underweight; use rallies toward the post-results gap as selling opportunities. Revisit only if management quantifies a recovery in ad targeting, which its metaverse-themed Super Bowl ad (WSJ) [[n1976]] does not.

catalysts.title: Tesla (TSLA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Tesla is recalling over 500,000 US vehicles to fix pedestrian warning sounds (Reuters) [[n1985]], California is suing over Black workers' discrimination allegations (Reuters) [[n1967]], and the company cut a steering component from some cars because of the chip shortage (CNBC) [[n1080]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock fell -2.95% to 904.55 USD and is -18.23% over twenty sessions from 1,106.22 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Risk to the bearish view: if chip workarounds lift deliveries, the stock can squeeze higher quickly.
Trade Expression

Underweight relative to XLY, where restaurant names with pricing power offer better earnings visibility. Cover if the stock reclaims 1,106.22 USD, the level of twenty sessions ago, which would show the market looking through recalls and litigation.

catalysts.title: Cameco (CCJ)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Cameco's plan to restart its McArthur River uranium mine (Global News) [[n0664]] suggests confidence that contract prices justify new supply. Producers normally restart idled capacity only when they expect term prices to clear their costs, so the decision reads as a statement about demand, not just about Cameco's own output.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Cameco fell -1.67% to 22.40 USD on the day but is +17.15% over five sessions; it remains -6.04% over twenty sessions from 23.84 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Risk: the restart itself adds pounds to the market before new contracts are signed.
Trade Expression
Buy pullbacks toward 22.40 USD; a close above 23.84 USD confirms a full recovery of the twenty-session loss. Exit if URA gives back its +10.94% five-session gain.

catalysts.title: Siemens (SIE.DE)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Siemens agreed to sell its logistics business to Koerber in a 1.15 billion euro deal (Reuters) [[n0745]] and is selling its 50% stake in the Valeo Siemens e-Automotive joint venture (Reuters) [[n0747]], simplifying the portfolio and releasing capital.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The shares rose +4.72% to 144.68 EUR and +5.74% over five sessions, but are still -4.50% over twenty sessions from 151.50 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-10). Risk: European cyclicals remain hostage to a Russia-Ukraine escalation.
Trade Expression

Hold long while the stock stays above 144.68 EUR; a close above 151.50 EUR signals a trend recovery. Siemens Mobility's 12-year contract for NCTD DMU vehicles (Siemens Mobility Global) [[n0846]] adds visible backlog that does not depend on the consumer cycle.
